goal: Users can run and maintain independently packaged Web, macOS, Windows, and Python ThesisForge products, with the desktop flow using one target-native frozen sidecar fully offline.
non_goals: Do not change parser, validator, template, compiler, bibliography, renderer, DOCX, or OOXML behavior.
Do not introduce another frontend/desktop stack, cloud dependency, account, database, AI, telemetry, updater, or Linux/mobile native release.
Do not publish, sign, notarize, upload, or spend money on release credentials.
Do not claim Windows package execution without native Windows runner evidence.
expected_evidence: Strict RED and GREEN for release configuration, target-specific sidecar naming, platform mismatch rejection, artifact isolation, and native bundle discovery
Frozen sidecar inspect, validate, preview, build, cancellation, and reopen smoke evidence with sockets blocked and credentials removed
Valid DOCX package and preserved prior-output checks from the frozen sidecar
Browser acceptance for populated, loading, empty, error, disabled, permission, dirty, canceled, and success states
Keyboard-only, labels, focus visibility, contrast, responsive resize, and reduced-motion checks
Independent Python wheel/sdist, Web production, macOS app/dmg, and Windows msi/nsis build evidence
Workflow/static tests proving macOS and Windows use native runners and do not relabel sidecars
Full frontend, Python, Ruff, pip, Cargo, distribution, strict OpenSpec, SpecNav, CodeGraph, JSON, and whitespace gates
README and maintenance instructions with capability differences, limitations, troubleshooting, signing/notarization gates, checksums, and artifact provenance
Six-domain verification inputs plus task report, spec review, and quality review
unsafe_assumptions: A host sidecar can be renamed for another target.
System Python fallback satisfies packaged offline operation.
A CI file proves Windows packaging without an executed run.
Browser-only accessibility evidence proves native package launch.
stop_condition: Stop if a platform needs a second frontend/service/protocol, offline desktop still requires system Python or network, cross-OS artifacts would be relabeled, release requires external signing/publishing credentials, or implementation would change compiler/rendering semantics.
